A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same OCO study, including the main text, supplementary Sections 7–9, and references. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the titles and arXiv version/date stamp; no material comparison gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD and full-spectrum OOD experiments, ablations, classification and statistical analyses (Tables 1–5), and supplementary attention and score-distribution results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original OOD and full-spectrum OOD experiments, ablations, classification and statistical analyses (Tables 1–5), and supplementary visual results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical slot-attention modeling, classification and reconstruction losses, co-occurrence grouping, and three scenario-specific detection scores.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k/200, SSB-hard, NINCO, iNaturalist, Textures, OpenImage-O, and ImageNet-v2/C/R. OOD, full-spectrum OOD, classification, and WordNet-analysis coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Energy, MaxLogit, SHE, NNguide, SCALE, NECO, FDBD, CoRP, and OODD with both backbones. The standard-classification comparison in Table 4 and MSP comparison in Figure 10 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The data subsets and sampling, ViT and DINOv2 backbones, 20-epoch fine-tuning, FPR95/AUROC evaluation, and object-centric classification criterion remain identical (Sections 4 and 8; Table 6).

E4.justification: The reconstruction-loss/scoring ablation, scenario and slot-count analyses, generalization and WordNet analyses, and supplementary attention and score-distribution studies are unchanged (Tables 3–5; Figures 3–10).

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same Spearman correlation and p-value reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 1 reports identical OCO mean FPR95/AUROC values of 47.26/86.04 with ViT and 38.70/87.75 with DINOv2 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, co-occurrence definition, model and scoring equations, and supplementary Dempster–Shafer formalism are identical (Sections 2–3 and 7). No assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The revised title preserves the claim of mitigating simplicity bias through object co-occurrence. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive scoring and handling semantic and covariate shifts.

C2.justification: The explanations linking performance to disentanglement and co-occurrence remain identical. Supplementary Section 9 retains the same limitations concerning fixed slot counts, over-segmentation, and small objects.

D1.justification: Implementation and training details in Section 4.1 and supplementary Section 8.3/Table 6, dataset descriptions, and the code-release link are unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 5, the cited works, and the positioning of OCO relative to earlier OOD detection and object-centric learning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The main and supplementary titles change from 'Divide and Conquer: Object Co-occurrence Helps Mitigate Simplicity Bias in OOD Detection' to 'Mitigating Simplicity Bias in OOD Detection through Object Co-occurrence Analysis.' The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; body prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All ten figures and six tables retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement. The revised titles occupy the same centered two-line heading areas, leaving the surrounding page layout unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 retitles the paper and updates the version/date stamp while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations, including the supplement. These editorial changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
